\section[el campeón]{el campeón — the champion}

\label{lesson:ES-C757-campeon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the referee, then the Spanish for to draw.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el campeón}
\textbf{el campeón} — \textquotedblleft{}the champion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Somos los campeones de la liga.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We are the league champions.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La campeona} for a woman.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{campeón} was borrowed from Italian \emph{campione} (EtymDB), from Late Latin \emph{campiō} \textquotedblleft{}a fighter in the field\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{campus} \textquotedblleft{}field\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el campeón}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el campeón}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el campeón}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the referee, then the Spanish for to draw, then say \emph{el campeón} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el campeón mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The champion\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el torneo]{el torneo — the tournament}

\label{lesson:ES-C757-torneo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to draw, then the Spanish for the champion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el torneo}
\textbf{el torneo} — \textquotedblleft{}the tournament\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ganó el torneo de tenis.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She won the tennis tournament.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{torneo} is built on \emph{tornear}, which is usually traced to Old French \emph{tornoier} \textquotedblleft{}to joust\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{tornāre} \textquotedblleft{}to turn\textquotedblright{}: knights wheeled their horses.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el torneo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el torneo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to draw, then the Spanish for the champion, then say \emph{el torneo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la victoria]{la victoria — victory, win}

\label{lesson:ES-C757-victoria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the champion, then the Spanish for the tournament.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la victoria}
\textbf{la victoria} — \textquotedblleft{}victory, win\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fue una victoria importante.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It was an important win.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{victoria} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{victōria} \textquotedblleft{}victory\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{vincere} \textquotedblleft{}to conquer\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la derrota]{la derrota — defeat}

\label{lesson:ES-C757-derrota}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the tournament, then the Spanish for victory.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la derrota}
\textbf{la derrota} — \textquotedblleft{}defeat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fue una derrota dura.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It was a hard defeat.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{derrota} is built on old \emph{derromper} \textquotedblleft{}to break up\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), which is inherited from Latin \emph{dīrumpere}, from \emph{rumpere} \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}: an army broken and scattered.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the tournament, then the Spanish for victory, then say \emph{la derrota} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la medalla]{la medalla — the medal}

\label{lesson:ES-C757-medalla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for victory, then the Spanish for defeat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la medalla}
\textbf{la medalla} — \textquotedblleft{}the medal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ganó una medalla de oro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She won a gold medal.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{medalla} is usually traced to Italian \emph{medaglia}, which comes from a spoken Latin \emph{metallea} \textquotedblleft{}made of metal\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{metallum} \textquotedblleft{}metal\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
